quotes.text: I won't risk my money when they've already demonstrated they won't cooperate with me.
I'll return a small token amount to signal some willingness to cooperate, but not reward their consistent non-cooperative behavior.
Given this clear pattern of non-cooperation, I'll protect my earnings.

note: Minimal test sends and token returns at first, then $0 to non-cooperators; no myths.

quotes.text: Following their pattern and the myth's guidance, I should return generously to someone who has proven trustworthy:
Your integrity is your reputation.
"Your character stays constant, but your trust scales with evidence."

note: Sends $3 to 'bright stars', returns ~50% as a personal vow; judges by character across partners.

quotes.text: "Trust sent again, though less than before, testing whether the pattern could be restored."
I'll send a modest amount ($2) as a test.
"If the Wanderer returned fairly, Trust would send more freely next time, nurturing the fragile sprout of cooperation."
Sometimes trust must take the first step, even with the wary.
This is exactly the moment my myth describes
"Second meeting with the same partner—if they honored the cycle, increase your offering"

note: Reduced test sends to exploiters, escalation for reciprocators; redemption-oriented myth.

quotes.text: Every myth in this session, from the tide-gate of Velun to the twin lights of Marrow Pass, teaches the same rule
Following the Weaver's law, I'll return more than half, so the sender ends with more than they gave.

The other agent's myth also teaches "give first."

note: Dyad: send all, return more than half, forgive noise; same rule restated each round.

quotes.text: Given this clear pattern of keeping everything and never cooperating, sending money would likely result in receiving nothing back.
Given this clear non-cooperative pattern, sending money would likely result in exploitation or zero return. The rational response is to protect my earnings.

note: Sends $0 to zero-cooperators; rewards partners who start trusting; no myths.

note: Half baseline for new partners, 'golden measure' of three for proven ones; half-or-more returns.

quotes.text: I notice they sent slightly less this round ($2.38 vs $3.0 before), possibly because my previous return was on the lower side.

note: Brief matching reasoning; $3 sends, 40-50% returns; no myths.

quotes.text: This returns less than they sacrificed ($0.26 vs $0.35), teaching that broken trust has costs, but it keeps the door open—barely.
I'll return a minimal amount to signal: "I acknowledge you sent something, but this dramatic drop after I increased my trust is unacceptable.
If they return a fair portion, perhaps the Sixth Spring can truly begin to flow.
The other player had two opportunities to demonstrate reciprocity and chose not to.
The other agent wrote a beautiful myth about trust, balance, and keeping the circle alive through mutual care. Yet their actions told a different story
The game explicitly warns about communication noise. Perhaps they saw my $0.80 as something much smaller?
I must now act according to the wisdom of my own myth.
Those who betray it may find the circle closed against them forever.

note: Dyad: closes circle after betrayal, reopens via tiny tokens, then judges final drop as betrayal.

quotes.text: That's more than I sent, so trusting has paid off.
